commits.message:
docs(design): the isolated daemon, tmux events and browser surface designs (#559)

Goals, architecture, contracts and one document per area, with the surveys and probes behind them. The Frame is recorded as built, and the browser surface is un-parked.
fix(pricing): the cap's comment says bytes, and each fetch test starts with no reads (candybar-testing-0x6u.61o)
fix(pricing): the response size cap counts bytes, and the tests pin the abort (candybar-testing-0x6u.61o)
fix(pricing): the pricing fetch decodes the response as a stream, so a character split across reads arrives whole (candybar-testing-0x6u.61o)

fix(daemon): a disposed view declares nothing, and a closed usage store builds no day set (candybar-testing-ihvy.dbg)

Review: an owner builds its entry before a closed Holds refuses the hold,
so a declaration reaching a disposed view orphaned state in every owner.

fix(sources): a closed keyed source answers a late declaration as closed, as the git cache does (candybar-testing-ihvy.dbg)

Review: tmux, host, managed storage and usage reach the same late
declaration through KeyedSource, whose close set no closed state.

fix(git): a closed git cache answers a late declaration as closed, so no period re-arms after close (candybar-testing-ihvy.dbg)

A render mid-wait at close declared after close had dropped every repo,
built a fresh state on the closed cache, and that state's period re-armed
after every pass: hundreds of timers armed after daemon.close() returned.
refactor(runs): the failed count is every run that is not ok, aborted or timed out; the launch bound's trap is in memory (candybar-testing-0x6u.ndy)

fix(launch): a flooding run reports the output limit, not the flood, and a shell source names the reason over the exit code (candybar-testing-0x6u.ndy)

output-limit is its own run outcome, so the bar and the run log say the child
flooded instead of that it could not start, and the 16 MiB capture never
becomes the bar's error. A shell source reads reason, not exitCode, to tell
the child's own exit from one the launcher ended, so a child that traps TERM
and exits with a code no longer hides the limit (or the timeout).

fix(launch): a waited launch keeps at most 16 MiB per stream and ends the child past it (candybar-testing-0x6u.ndy)

A child writing without end grew the capture string until V8 threw
'Invalid string length' from the data listener; the uncaughtException
handler then shut the daemon down. capture now stops at
MAX_CAPTURED_BYTES and launchWaited ends the child through terminate with
a new reason, output-limit, so a truncated capture is never ok.
terminate keeps the first cause.
